title: Termination-of-resuscitation rules in a physician-based emergency medical services system: external validation using the German Resuscitation Registry
summary:
In case of cardiac arrest outside a hospital, emergency medical personnel must decide whether resuscitation attempts should be continued or stopped. Decision rules have been developed to help identify patients who have very little chance of survival. However, most of these rules have been studied in other countries, and it remains unclear how reliably they work in the German emergency medical services system.
This study will analyse existing data from the German Resuscitation Registry. It will include adults who received resuscitation attempts from emergency medical services following cardiac arrest outside a hospital. For each case, researchers will retrospectively determine whether the decision rules would have recommended stopping or continuing resuscitation. These recommendations will then be compared with whether the patients actually survived until discharge from hospital.
Of particular importance is the number of patients who survived despite a rule recommending that resuscitation should be stopped. The study will also examine whether the reliability of the rules differs between patient groups and what their potential impact on resuscitation practices and transport to hospital might be.
The aim is to improve our understanding of the safety and reliability of these decision rules in the German emergency medical services system.

interventions.name:
Retrospective registry-based cohort of adult patients (≥18 years) with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in whom resuscitation was attempted or continued by emergency medical services. Data will be obtained from the German Resuscitation Registry.

Established termination-of-resuscitation (TOR) rules

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) documented in the German Resuscitation Registry, with resuscitation initiated or continued by emergency medical services (EMS).

Patients will be included irrespective of the presumed cause of cardiac arrest or whether the arrest was witnessed by EMS personnel.
Exclusion criteria:
Primary declaration of death without resuscitation initiated or continued by emergency medical services (EMS).

Cases with unknown survival status at hospital discharge will be excluded from the primary validation analysis. Missing data on individual TOR criteria will result in exclusion from the primary validation of the respective TOR rule.
